stories.headline: Codelco shareholder meeting erupts in public clash between Kast ministers and outgoing board chair Pacheco
stories.summary: At Codelco's April 20 annual shareholders' meeting — the last chaired by Máximo Pacheco — Finance Minister Quiroz and Mining Minister Mas publicly challenged Pacheco's management record, citing a 20% output decline over his tenure and demanding self-criticism. Pacheco defended the company's performance and denied any crisis, while privatization speculation emerged and was subsequently walked back by the government. Pacheco later visited former President Boric to discuss Codelco's future, a meeting read as an expression of political support.

stories.headline: Kast submits sweeping economic 'megarreforma' to Congress, relying on PDG votes amid Chile Vamos ambivalence
stories.summary: President Kast signed and submitted the Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional — a roughly 40-measure omnibus bill combining a corporate tax cut from 27% to 23%, fiscal adjustment, and post-wildfire reconstruction funds — to the Chamber of Deputies on April 22. The government secured a pivotal but contentious agreement with the PDG's Franco Parisi for the bill's initial vote, while Chile Vamos expressed discomfort at being outmaneuvered and opposition parties announced plans to challenge the bill at the Constitutional Tribunal on procedural grounds.

stories.headline: Kast delivers combative speech against Boric legacy at RN council, prompting opposition rebuttals
stories.summary: At the Renovación Nacional general council on April 25, President Kast labeled the Boric government a 'disaster' across employment, security, and public administration, stating 'there is no figure where they can say they did well.' The speech drew immediate reactions from former ministers Jackson and Cataldo, from Boric himself (who declined to respond directly), and from Metropolitan Governor Orrego who said Kast was 'dividing Chile.'

stories.headline: Criteria poll: Kast approval nudges up to 38% while disapproval holds at 49%
stories.summary: The April 26 Criteria survey showed Kast's approval rating rising one point to 38%, while disapproval remained stable at 49% and 13% expressed no opinion. The poll also probed attitudes toward the Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional and Michelle Bachelet's potential candidacy for a UN post.

stories.headline: Kast leads second-anniversary ceremony for 'Héroes de Arauco' carabineros killed in 2024
stories.summary: President Kast traveled to Los Álamos in the Biobío Region on April 26 to mark the second anniversary of the murder of Carabineros Sergio Arévalo, Carlos Cisternas, and Misael Vidal, who were killed in Cañete in April 2024. Kast praised the life sentences handed to the three convicted brothers and called for tougher sanctions against attacks on public servants.

stories.headline: Chile and United States sign bilateral agreements on critical minerals and organized crime cooperation
stories.summary: On April 20–21, Chile and the US signed two agreements: a memorandum of understanding on critical minerals investment (copper, lithium, rare earths) and an updated security cooperation agreement providing $1 million in US funding to support joint FBI–PDI operations against organized crime. The signing was criticized by left-wing media as ceding Chilean sovereignty over resource decisions to Washington.

stories.headline: Proposed cuts to school feeding and child health programs trigger political backlash against Kast government
stories.summary: A leaked Hacienda memo proposing to discontinue the JUNAEB school meals program and child health checks in schools sparked a political firestorm. Kast defended the proposed cuts by attacking the Boric government's handling of the programs, while Finance Minister Quiroz faced pressure from both the opposition (which demanded a special congressional session) and from within Chile Vamos. The government reframed the issue as management reform rather than budget cuts.

stories.headline: Minister Poduje's claim that government does not 'rest on Chile Vamos' sparks coalition tensions
stories.summary: Housing Minister Iván Poduje stated that the Kast government 'does not rest on Chile Vamos,' contradicting RN's depiction of itself as the governing pillar. The remark drew sharp reactions from RN, UDI, and Evópoli, reopening questions about the government's coalition strategy. The episode coincided with a broader debate about whether Chile Vamos had 'run its cycle,' triggered by UDI deputy Cretton, and with calls by Kast himself to build a wider coalition including the Partido Republicano.

stories.headline: Chile and Bolivia's foreign ministers meet at border crossing in bid to restore diplomatic relations after 50 years
stories.summary: Chilean Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna and Bolivian Chancellor Fernando Aramayo met at the Chungará–Tambo Quemado border crossing on April 23, later continuing in La Paz and Santa Cruz, calling the encounter 'fundamental' to restoring relations suspended since 1962. Both governments announced a bilateral consular commission and initial economic agreements including an air services accord. President Kast expressed interest in visiting Bolivia.

stories.headline: Kast's private La Moneda lunch with university friends triggers Contraloría review and public apology
stories.summary: President Kast initially joked about and then acknowledged committing an 'error of ignorance' after hosting a private lunch for some 50 former law school classmates at the Palacio de La Moneda, prompting a Contraloría inquiry into whether public funds were used. Kast said the cost was borne personally, promised it would not recur, and said the Contraloría's inquiry had been answered.

stories.headline: Appointment of ex-Boric minister to San Antonio hospital subdirector post sparks political controversy and mass resignations
stories.summary: The naming of former Boric Social Development Minister Jeanette Vega as medical subdirector of the Claudio Vicuña Hospital in San Antonio provoked a political row, with Partido Republicano legislators calling it inappropriate. The hospital director was subsequently removed for 'loss of confidence,' triggering the resignation of approximately 20 physicians. PPD accused Republicanos of imposing 'political blacklists.'

stories.headline: Chile moves to speed mining permit approvals and streamline investment framework ahead of $100 billion pipeline
stories.summary: Economy and Mining Minister Daniel Mas announced plans to simplify approximately 200 procedures and cut permit processing times by 30% under a new sectoral permitting framework, without lowering environmental standards. The government also appointed economist Pablo Eguiguren to lead the Office of Sectoral Authorizations as its key 'anti-permisología' official.
